text:
alex: Heads-up — us-west2 had two spot drains in the 06:00–07:00 window. Both caused ~90s tail spikes and a handful of routing 503s. Thinking we should try a proactive eviction-hedging approach: small always-on on-demand lane + extend drain window to allow backfill. Opinions? :thinking:

meera: Can you share numbers? how many GPUs affected and what percent of traffic fell back?

alex: ~32 preemptible GPUs drained across 3 AZs. About 2.3% of requests experienced retries, p99 latency jumped ~120ms, and a few short 503s for heavy contexts.

chris: I like hedging. Proposal sketch: keep a min_on_demand_per_az = 4 (config below) and a drain_safety_window = 45s to allow KV/prefix cache warmup on backfill. Also proactively mark backfill lanes with lower packing density. Example YAML snippet:

```yaml
pool_mix:
  on_demand_min: 4
  spot_ratio: 0.92
  backfill_mode: true
  drain_safety_window_s: 45
  prewarm_on_demand: true
```

chris: Mechanism: when a spot eviction signal appears, route new short-lived sessions to the on-demand min lanes and pause scheduling heavy long-context jobs to avoid cold-KV storms.

meera: Main worry: cache invalidation and network surge when many sessions rehydrate KV caches into on-demand nodes. We need a staggered reconnect/backoff and a per-node token bucket.

chris: Agreed. Plan: add a reconnect jitter and token bucket per node; also keep a small prefix cache snapshot replicated to on-demand nodes for last-5m keys. That reduces warmup I/O.

tia: Cost tradeoff? If we hold 4 GPUs per AZ on-demand steady-state, what delta do we expect on monthly spend?

chris: Quick ballpark: on-demand baseline for these lanes +4% cost in exchange for cutting 503 risk by ~30–40% during drain storms. I can run a proper estimate using last 30d utilization data.

alex: One more operational piece — drain window length. Current drains are immediate preempt notices, so nodes go away fast. If we implement graceful drains with a 45s safety_window we need a changed signal from cloud (or intercept preemption webhook) and delay eviction for that time. That buys us time to re-route and backfill.

infra-bot: [us-west2-a] spot-drain detected at 2026-03-18T06:12:09Z (id i-0abcd). Suggested graceful-drain window 30s applied. :rotating_light:

meera: Also: ensure dedicated/private customers' QoS not impacted. We should gate hedging by tenant priority. If a dedicated tenant needs capacity we shrink hedging pool first.

chris: Yep. Policy: hedging only active for non-SLA background lanes; canary toggle per-region. We'll add feature flag hedging:enabled:{region}.

alex: Action items: (1) chris -> simulate 45s drain_safety_window + token-bucket reconnect in test cluster and measure 503 reduction (due 2 days). (2) chris -> cost estimate for on_demand_min at 2/4/6 per AZ (due 3 days). (3) meera -> run chaos test with staggered reconnect to validate KV warming and network egress (due 4 days). tia -> review pricing impact and flag to sales if dedicated SLAs affected.

chris: will start tests now. posting quick command we used in staging to simulate drain:

```bash
kubectl label node $NODE drain-test=true
# simulate preempt webhook
curl -X POST $INTERNAL_PREEMPT_ENDPOINT -d '{"node":"'$NODE'","eta_s":45}'
```

meera: thx. if results look good we can rollout hedging as a region-level opt-in. :thumbsup:

alex: agreed. if hedging cuts retries and 503s it's worth the small steady cost.

tia: ping me when chris has the numbers — i'll run projections for Qtrly spend impact.

chris: noted, will attach logs + prometheus graphs in the test PR.

alex: cool. let's treat this as a safety feature we can toggle per-region. Appreciate the quick sync. :wave:
